explanation: Greedily choose each line before assigning spaces. Nonfinal lines divide their available spaces among gaps, putting remainders on the left; the final line uses single spaces and right padding.
timeComplexity: O(total output characters + number of words)
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The greedy end index is the longest consecutive word prefix fitting with mandatory single spaces. For a nonfinal line, dividing the remaining spaces by the gap count assigns every required space, and distributing the remainder to earlier gaps implements leftmost preference. The final-line branch and right padding give every returned line exactly L characters.
walkthrough: With words ["a","bb","c","dddd"] and width 8, the first three words fit but adding "dddd" does not. Their four letters leave four spaces, split as two per gap, yielding "a  bb  c". The final word becomes "dddd    ".
edgeCases: A single-word line receives all padding on its right.
The final line uses single inter-word spaces.
No output line may exceed or fall short of the requested width.
